audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Garen/Skill/Skill/Garen, which matches neither the mirror nor its own why-text.
audit.why: The mirror (jayce__garen) is already audited and settled on Levels 1-3 Jayce, level 4 onward Garen, two items back to Skill. The page's own whys already say Jayce owns Level 3 ('poke and disengage faster than you can catch him') and that Garen owns Level 6 and first item — so three of the four token flips just bring the chart back in line with the prose that was already there.
audit.corrected: Chart set as one atomic group to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Garen/Garen/Garen/Skill, with whys[6] rewritten so two items reads as even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer stated what Decisive Strike actually does against Jayce, and the stance swap was never named as an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: The mirror recorded the decisive interaction from the other side: Garen's Q breaks Shock Blast's slow, speeds him in, resets his own auto, and its silence denies the stance swap. Restating it from this side costs nothing and keeps the two pages consistent. Separately, Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer is a 6s stance swap that resets his attack — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell.
audit.corrected: Slow-break and stance-swap silence written into report[5] and the commit line; the reset tell into dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast was given a 6s cooldown; the packet also logged 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 6s is the rank-6 value, reached only with the ultimate levelled and the ability maxed. At rank 1 it is 16 seconds, and that gap is the entire early-lane punish window. Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Real 16s-at-rank-1 figure written into report[5] and dosFull[0].t; Thundering Blow's 20s into Common Mistakes.
